extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO filers (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing USPTO publication of patent applications (including sequence listings), use and rescission of nonpublication requests, notices of foreign filings, republication requests, and related filing-format requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lengthy Sequence Listing / Sequence Listing XML publication
rubrics_metrics.description: File size is used to determine if the 'Sequence Listing XML' is a lengthy 'Sequence Listing XML.' Lengthy 'Sequence Listings' or 'Sequence Listing XMLs' will be published only in electronic form on the homepage (https://seqdata.uspto.gov). The patent or patent application publication will include a statement that the patent or application contains a lengthy 'Sequence Listing' or 'Sequence Listing XML' section (as applicable) and a hyperlink to the webpage containing the 'Sequence Listing' or 'Sequence Listing XML'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to MPEP §§ 2419 et seq. and 2435; lengthy sequence listings are not printed in the paper publication but made available electronically with a hyperlink in the publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid filing preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should not file any preliminary amendment with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting applications without accompanying preliminary amendments reduces Office processing and helps ensure correct printing of patent application publications. If a preliminary amendment is present on the filing date, it becomes part of the original disclosure under 37 CFR 1.115(a)(1) and will be included in the patent application publication. Generally a substitute specification (excluding claims) is required for preliminary amendments to the specification (other than claims). Applicants are advised to incorporate desired amendments into the text of the specification (including a new set of claims) rather than filing preliminary amendments, even in continuation or divisional applications (subject to rules on new matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment formatting and substitute specification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a preliminary amendment present on the filing date is not in a format usable for publication, the Office will issue a notice requiring the applicant to submit the amendment in a format usable for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, a substitute specification (excluding claims) is required for any preliminary amendments to the specification (other than the claims) that are present on the filing date. Although a substitute specification is a usable format for publication, applicants should avoid filing a substitute specification with the application because the application size fee will be calculated based on the application papers including the clean version and marked-up version of the substitute specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporating amendments in continuations/divisionals (no new matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a continuation or divisional application, a new specification reflecting amendments made in the parent application may be submitted together with a copy of the oath or declaration from the previously filed application so long as no new matter is included in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific references to prior applications required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 and 37 CFR 1.78(a) for applications filed on or after September 16, 2012 may be submitted in an application data sheet (ADS) rather than in a preliminary amendment. If the specific reference is submitted in a preliminary amendment, a substitute specification will not be required if the preliminary amendment only adds or amends a benefit claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for republication to correct publication errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications with poor quality text may lead to errors in the patent application publication; correction of these errors and inclusion of desired amendments into the text of the originally-filed specification and drawings will only occur if the applicant files a request for republication under 37 CFR 1.221(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors will not be corrected by the Office in a corrected publication under 37 CFR 1.221(b). See MPEP § 1130 for further procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices printing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices, other than those containing 'Sequence Listings' (for apps filed before July 1, 2022), 'Sequence Listing XMLs' (for apps filed on/after July 1, 2022), or 'Large Tables', are not printed if they are contained on pages located after the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application includes multiple claim sets in the specification, the Office may treat pages located after the first set of claims as appendices. Computer program listings may be printed if included in the specification before the claims, but 'Computer Program Listing Appendices' submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system or on a read-only optical disc in accordance with 37 CFR 1.96(c) and 37 CFR 1.52(e) are not printed as part of the patent or patent application publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of amended application copy submitted via USPTO patent electronic filing system for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: At applicant’s option, a patent application publication may be based upon a copy of the application (specification, drawings and oath or declaration) as amended, provided applicant supplies such a copy in compliance with the USPTO patent electronic filing system requirements within specified timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amended copy must be supplied in compliance with EFS requirements (e.g., set forth in the Legal Framework for Patent Electronic System) within one month of the mailing date of the first Office communication confirmation number for the application, or fourteen months of the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought under title 35, whichever is later (37 CFR 1.215(c)). If the copy submitted under 37 CFR 1.215(c) does not comply with EFS requirements, the Office will publish per 37 CFR 1.215(a). If the copy was untimely, the Office may still use it if received before the Office has started the publication process. See the Electronic Business Center for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of applicant information (37 CFR 1.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent application is filed pursuant to 37 CFR 1.46, the patent application publication will include the name of the assignee, person to whom the inventor is under an obligation to assign the invention, or person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The information must be provided on the application data sheet (ADS) filed with the application. If applicant information is corrected or updated in accordance with 37 CFR 1.46(c) after filing, the corrected or updated information may be used if the information is recognized by the Office before the technical preparation for the publication has begun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee information submission and publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, if the applicant would like assignee data to be published, the assignee data must be submitted on the application data sheet (ADS). For applications filed before September 16, 2012, the assignee data may be provided on the application transmittal letter or the ADS filed with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing assignee information on the transmittal letter or ADS does not substitute for compliance with any requirement of 37 CFR Part 3 to have an assignment recorded by the Office. If the assignee data is recorded only with the Assignment Recordation Branch, the information will not be published as part of the patent application publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in applicant/assignee information are not 'material mistakes' for correction except by republication
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors in applicant or assignee information printed on the publication are not considered material mistakes by the Office under 37 CFR 1.211(b) or 1.221(b) (e.g., errors in the assignee’s name).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such errors may only be corrected if applicant files a request for republication under 37 CFR 1.211(a) or 37 CFR 1.221(a). See MPEP § 1130.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication request statutory requirements (37 CFR 1.213(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonpublication request will cause the application not to be published only if the following are satisfied: (1) the request is submitted with the application upon filing; (2) the request states in a conspicuous manner that the application is not to be published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b); (3) the request contains a certification that the invention disclosed has not been and will not be the subject of an application filed in another country or under a multilateral international agreement that requires publication at eighteen months after filing; and (4) the request is signed in compliance with § 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use Form PTO/SB/35 (Nonpublication Request) to ensure correct language and conspicuous presentation. A nonpublication request lacking the statutory language or not conspicuously presented (e.g., buried as one paragraph among many) will not be accepted or recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual inquiry and affirmative intent required before signing nonpublication certification (37 CFR 11.18(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The person signing the nonpublication certification must make an actual inquiry consistent with 37 CFR 11.18(b) to determine (A) the application has not been the subject of a foreign/international application requiring 18-month publication, and (B) the signer’s intent at the time is that the U.S. application will not be the subject of such a foreign/international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nonpublication request cannot be made based on lack of knowledge, past practices, or statistical tendencies (e.g., filing foreign counterparts for fewer than 50% of U.S. apps). The applicant must have affirmative intent not to file counterpart applications that would trigger eighteen-month publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication request timing and filing mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonpublication request must be filed upon filing of the application; this is a statutory requirement and cannot be waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a nonpublication request filed with a conversion request to convert a provisional to a nonprovisional will not be accepted as the nonprovisional would be accorded the provisional's filing date. The nonpublication request must be included with the application papers and cannot be filed separately in a different package on the same date. If the filing receipt shows a projected publication date despite a recognized nonpublication request, contact the Office promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate nonpublication requests and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonpublication request is inappropriate if a counterpart foreign or international application that requires eighteen-month publication has already been filed (even if later abandoned), or if the certification is otherwise improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an improper certification is filed, the Office will not accept the nonpublication request and will assign a projected publication date, notifying the applicant and providing a non-extendable 30-day period to provide a satisfactory explanation. Failure to provide a satisfactory explanation will result in publication. An applicant or representative who makes a false statement may violate 37 CFR 11.18(b) and other disciplinary rules; applicants should promptly rescind improper requests and contact the Application Assistance Unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission of a nonpublication request (37 CFR 1.213(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may rescind a previously-filed nonpublication request at any time. A request to rescind must (1) identify the application; (2) state conspicuously that the nonpublication request is rescinded; and (3) be signed in compliance with § 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/36 may be used to rescind a nonpublication request and to provide notice of foreign filing. If the rescission occurs before or on the date a counterpart application is filed in the USPTO, the nonpublication request will be treated as annulled and the application will be treated as if no nonpublication request was made. Applicants are strongly encouraged to provide a notice of foreign filing when rescinding in anticipation of foreign filing. A rescission is not a paper under 37 CFR 1.8(a), so the USPTO uses the actual date of receipt per 37 CFR 1.6 to determine timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of foreign filing requirement and 45-day timing (37 CFR 1.213(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant who submitted a nonpublication request subsequently files an application directed to the same invention in a foreign country or under a multilateral international agreement that requires eighteen-month publication, the applicant must notify the USPTO of such foreign filing not later than 45 days after the date of the foreign filing. Failure to timely notify will result in abandonment of the U.S. application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/36 (revision April 2001 or later) may be used to both rescind a nonpublication request and provide notice of foreign filing. The benefit of a certificate of mailing or transmission under 37 CFR 1.8 will be given to a notice of foreign filing. If the 45th day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday in D.C., filing on the next business day is timely. After a rescission or notice is received, the Office will schedule the application for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office processing and publication after rescission or notice of foreign filing
rubrics_metrics.description: After either a rescission of a nonpublication request or a notice of foreign filing is received, the Office will enter the rescission or notice into the Office Pre-Examination System to schedule the application for publication and will send a notice informing the applicant of the projected publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application will be published promptly after expiration of the 18-month period from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought, or as soon as practicable after mailing the notice. See 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment and revival for failure to provide timely notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application abandoned pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii) for failure to timely notify the Office of the filing of a corresponding foreign application may be revived only pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.137 must be accompanied by: (1) the reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee; (3) any terminal disclaimer (and fee) required; and (4) a statement that the entire delay in filing the required reply was unintentional. For abandonment for failure to notify the Office of a foreign filing, the notification of such filing in a foreign country may meet the reply requirement, but filing a petition does not stay any period for reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redacted publication option when foreign-filed applications are less extensive
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant has filed applications in one or more foreign countries and such foreign-filed applications corresponding to the U.S. application are less extensive than the U.S. application, the applicant may submit a redacted copy of the U.S. application eliminating any part or description not also contained in the corresponding foreign applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may only publish the redacted copy unless the redacted copy is not received within 16 months after the earliest effective filing date for which a benefit is sought. The provisions of section 154(d) will not apply to a claim if the description published in the redacted application does not enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the subject matter of the claim.
